notes: RAISED 90 -> 94 on 2026-10-25, after the product-only climb (#6131 changed the measure; work packages #6133-#6153 added tests). Main reads 94.12% on that basis (run 40243396144, main@d465cbf1, gate-coverage-3.12-1), so 94 is the floor of the measured value (the fleet's convention: the jitter tolerance lives in warn_drop, 1.0, not in the floor); the guard therefore reports a breach only below 93.0%, which is 1.12 points under the reading. A ratchet: raise it as coverage rises, never lower it to make a run pass. Readings before 2026-10-25 are on the old all-files basis and are not comparable. EARLIER NOTE (2026-10-25, when the measure changed): UNCHANGED at 90.0 on purpose (2026-10-25). The coverage MEASURE changed to product code only: [tool.coverage.run] source in pyproject.toml now limits it to src/, streamlit_app/, design-system/ and analysis/, and tests, scripts/, tools/ and .github/ no longer count (the target is product code at or above 90%). On the old basis (every imported file, the tests' own 98% among them) main read 91.12%; on this basis the same code reads roughly 84-85% (84.85% from the old payload's product files, 84.19% once never-imported files join), so the guard is expected to report a breach until the product code is tested up to the target. That breach is true, not a regression: nothing was lost, the measure got stricter.
